title: regional-prefetch-degrade-controller: probabilistic prefetch + graceful fallback to reduce cross-region tail latency
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: During a recent cross-region incident we observed amplified 95/99th tail latency when the primary region experienced transient CPU pressure. Existing region-failover and global circuit-breakers reliably keep availability high but cause large volume of cold RPCs to remote regions which inflates tail latency and cost. This PR introduces a regional prefetch + degradation controller that: (1) does low-cost probabilistic prefetches of likely hot KV/cache prefixes into candidate failover regions, (2) exposes an admission policy that enforces soft SLO targets by probabilistic dropping/queue-priority when regional SLO budget is exhausted, and (3) provides a fast fallback cache layer that serves short-lived stale responses for specific workload classes.

Goals: reduce cross-region tail latency amplification and cost during regional pressure, provide an operable rollout path (canary flag + gradual ramp), and fix a correctness bug found in the existing failover path where prefetched KV could be used without the right cache-tagging causing stale-visibility regressions (incident SUP-4421).

What this PR changes (high level):
- New controller: pkg/runtime/prefetch_controller.go — core implementation of probabilistic prefetch, admission sampling, and TTL tagging for fallback cache.
- Runtime hooks: pkg/runtime/fallback_cache.go — fast in-memory fallback cache with strict tag-based visibility checks and metrics.
- Admission policy config: configs/runtime/prefetch.yaml — runtime knobs for sampling rate, SLO thresholds, and penalty decay windows.
- Canary deployment: deploy/k8s/overlays/prefetch-canary.yaml — a controlled canary install with feature-gate and reduced sampling for 10% of traffic.
- Tests & turbometrics: test/integration/prefetch_e2e_test.go, ci/scripts/run-prefetch-smoke.sh
- Docs & runbook: docs/runbooks/regional-prefetch-fallback.md and notes to on-call about rollback toggles.

Checklist: - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] canary deployment config - [x] runbook + dashboard links - [x] security review (no new credentials/KMS) - [x] perf benchmark run against internal staging (p95 improved by ~18% in a simulated failover scenario)

Commits summary: 3 commits — initial controller and cache implementation; add config + canary yaml; fix stale-tag race condition after review and add additional unit tests.

Testing & telemetry: local and CI tests included. Canary run for 72 hours in us-west-2 with 10% sampling showed reduced cross-region p95 by ~18% and reduced remote-token cost by ~22% for the injected pressure workload. Telemetry added: prefetch_attempts, prefetch_hits, admission_drops, fallback_serve_latency, stale_tag_errors. Added a Grafana dashboard link to the runbook and a Prometheus alert: prefallback_error_rate > 0.5% for 5m.

Rollout plan: enable feature-gate off by default; start canary 10% traffic with sampling 1% prefetch for 72 hours; if stable, increment sampling to 10% then 25% across non-critical namespaces; finally enable admission policy with conservative thresholds and monitor SLO burn. Full production ramp requires sign-off from SRE and runtime owners.

Why it's different from prior work: unlike previous PRs that focused on hard load-shedding or regional circuit-breakers, this PR adds a low-cost proactive strategy (probabilistic prefetch) combined with soft admission that aims to keep tail latencies bounded without full failover. The fallback cache ensures graceful degradation to slightly stale but available results for low-consistency workloads.

review_comments: Aaron Patel: Suggest moving TTL and tag checks into a shared util to avoid duplication with ringbuffer cache. Also saw a race on the prefetchedItem.flags access; please add RW lock.

release_notes: Add regional probabilistic prefetch controller + soft admission policy and a fast fallback cache to reduce cross-region tail latency and cost during regional pressure. Rollout via canary; enabled by feature-gate. Contains a hotfix for stale-tag visibility bug (SUP-4421).
canary_plan: Canary 10% traffic (us-west-2), 72h minimum; sampling=1% initially -> 10% -> 25%; monitor prefallback_error_rate, admission_drops, prefetch_waste; rollback by disabling feature-gate or setting sampling=0%.
hotfix_rationale: Fixes SUP-4421: previously prefetched items could be served without the proper visibility tag during fast KV writes. This caused stale responses under rare interleavings. The fix tags prefetched entries atomically and adds a small validation on serve.
notes_for_oncall: If alerts fire (prefallback_error_rate > 0.5% or stale_tag_errors > 0), immediately set 'prefetch.enabled=false' in runtime config or scale down canary overlay; contact Maya Chen and SRE rotation.
risk_profile: low-to-medium: prefetch sampling is probabilistic and off by default; fallback cache only targets low-consistency classes; the main risk is prefallback_waste increasing downstream cost, mitigated by telemetry and conservative defaults.
